title: 1960 AHSME Problem 22
statement: The equality \((x+m)^2-(x+n)^2=(m-n)^2,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are unequal non-zero constants, is satisfied by \(x=am+bn\) where:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(a\) and \(b\) each have a unique non-zero value

solutions.text:
Factoring and using \(m\ne n\) gives \[ \begin{gathered} (m-n)(2x+m+n)\\ {}=(m-n)^2. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(2x+m+n=m-n,\) so \(x=-n.\) Thus \(a=0\) and \(b=-1,\) a unique nonzero value.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Factor the difference of the two squares
Cancel the nonzero factor \(m-n\) and solve for \(x\)
